description: We are a software development team from Dushanbe building VITA, a health self-monitoring system for astronauts on long space missions. The app tracks vital signs, sleep, exercise, radiation dose, mood and alertness, compares them with each astronaut's own preflight baseline, and tells the crew what to do next, fully on board. Super Intelligence (SI) tools were used to assist with code and text; all design decisions and the final review were made by the team.
summary: VITA is a daily health self-check for astronauts on long-duration missions. In about two minutes a crew member logs vitals, sleep, exercise, radiation dose, mood and a five-tap alertness test, or receives them automatically from a wearable sensor shirt over Bluetooth. VITA compares every value with the astronaut's own preflight baseline rather than a population average, scores five body systems (cardiovascular, bone and muscle, immune, mind and fatigue, radiation), and returns a readiness score with concrete, prioritized actions and the reason for each. All scoring runs on board, so a communication delay of up to 20 minutes to Earth changes nothing; a short report goes to the flight surgeon when a link is available. Thresholds are anchored to published NASA references: the 600 mSv career radiation limit (NASA-STD-3001), the 1.84 mSv/day transit dose measured by MSL RAD, bone loss of 1 to 1.5% per month, and in-flight sleep data. This matters because on a Mars mission crews must detect slow changes in their own bodies before they become emergencies.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

VITA is a self-monitoring tool for crews on long-duration missions, built for the case where no doctor is on board and Earth is up to 20 minutes away. Each day the astronaut completes a two-minute check-in: resting heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, body temperature, body mass, sleep, resistive and aerobic exercise, dosimeter reading, mood, stress, symptoms, and a five-tap reaction-time test. Readings can also arrive automatically from a wearable sensor shirt (ECG, breathing, skin temperature, SpO2) over Bluetooth Low Energy.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Personal baseline: every measurement is compared with the astronaut's own preflight values, because a normal heart rate or reaction time differs from person to person.

2. Five system scores (0 to 100): cardiovascular, bone and muscle, immune, mind and fatigue, radiation. Each uses 3- to 7-day averages so one bad day does not raise a false alarm, while a week-long drift does.

3. Readiness score: the mean of the five scores weighted toward the weakest system, so one failing system is never hidden by good averages.

4. Recommended actions: every flag comes with the reason and one concrete action, ordered by urgency (for example, a dose spike above 4 mSv/day sends the crew to the storm shelter; resistive exercise under 45 min/day schedules a session).

5. Report: one button produces a plain-text summary for the flight surgeon, sent when a link is available.

NASA REFERENCE VALUES

Career radiation limit 600 mSv and short-term solar particle event limit 250 mSv (NASA-STD-3001); transit dose rate 1.84 mSv/day measured by the MSL RAD instrument; bone density loss of 1 to 1.5% per month without countermeasures and about 2 hours of daily exercise on the ISS (NASA Human Research Program); 8.5 h scheduled versus about 6 h actual sleep in flight (Barger et al., Lancet Neurology, 2014).

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Crews see slow, silent changes such as bone loss, sleep debt, rising resting heart rate or accumulating dose early, and know what to do without waiting for Earth. The same approach can support Antarctic stations, submarines and remote clinics.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Web app in HTML, CSS and JavaScript (works offline on a cabin tablet); REST API in Node.js and Express; PostgreSQL database with tables for crew baselines, daily check-ins and sensor readings; Docker Compose for one-command deployment. Code: https://github.com/mirzo6049-sys/vita

CREATIVITY AND CONSIDERATIONS

Baseline-relative scoring instead of fixed population thresholds; offline-first design for communication delay; actions instead of raw warnings; manual entry kept as a fallback if a sensor fails; light and dark themes and large touch targets for use in a cabin.

LIMITATIONS

Crew data and the sensor stream in the demo are simulated around the published reference values. Score weights are the team's own and need review by flight medicine. This is a research prototype, not a medical device.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) USE

Super Intelligence (SI) tools (a large language model) were used to help write code, interface text and presentation text. All design decisions, reference values and the final review were made by the team.

TRANSPARENT METHOD

The app lists every scoring rule with its basis under Reference data, and a mission phase selector switches the reference dose rate between Mars transit (1.84 mSv/day) and the Mars surface (0.64 mSv/day), both measured by MSL RAD.

30-SECOND VIDEO DEMO

https://github.com/mirzo6049-sys/vita/blob/main/docs/vita-demo-30s.mp4

Live app: https://novacode.myspaceproject.app/ (code: https://github.com/mirzo6049-sys/vita)

Team Novacode: Mirzorahmat Safarzoda, Idigul Kiyamova (Dushanbe, Tajikistan). The body-system video loops in the app were supplied by the team.
